maria (runtime): Hey team — I ran a canary for the multipool packing changes + new allocator heuristics. Observed a ~12% median token latency regression for small chat flows when KV-cache misses triggered model swaps.

adesh (eng-runtime): Can you paste the perf trace and clarify if this was cold-start swap activity or repeated steady-state evictions?

maria (runtime): Steady state primarily. Quick snippet from the sampling run (aggregated):
```
kvcache_hit_rate: 78%
swap_ops_per_s: 2.1
avg_token_latency_ms: 79 (baseline 70)
median_gpu_mem_allocs_s: 84
most_common_kernel: attention_fwd_v2
```

tomas (perf): swap_ops looks high for that mix. What allocator config did you use? slab vs continuous? workspace sizing?

maria (runtime): Trying a hybrid-slab allocator with a small per-request workspace. Config excerpt: 
```
packing:
  mode: multipool
allocator:
  type: hybrid-slab
  workspace_mb: 48
  reserve_fraction: 0.05
batching:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  latency_slo_ms: 50
reuse_buffers: false
```

sophia (ml-infra): The pattern smells like cross-model fragmentation + aggressive KV eviction. When two mid-size models interleave, soft-partitioning ends up forcing temporary kernel buffers into swap.

adesh (eng-runtime): Two quick ideas: 1) try pinning KV pages for small-chat models (soft pin) and 2) reduce workspace to force more compact kernel choices. Kernel selection sometimes picks larger temporaries when workspace is abundant.

maria (runtime): I experimented with soft-slices (0.2/0.6/0.2) and saw less direct eviction but more fragmentation overall. Kernel selector started choosing unfused kernels with bigger temp buffers.

ci-bot: deploy success: allocator-experiment-20240321 -> canary (3 nodes) :white_check_mark:

tomas (perf): We should capture per-kernel high-water memory and kernel names in traces. Also add kvcache eviction events to the perf logs so we can correlate swap_ops -> kernel decisions.

maria (runtime): Did a quick A/B: enabling buffer reuse (reuse_buffers=true) reduced swap_ops to ~0.6/s and median latency back to ~71ms, but tail latency for long-sequence models increased and throughput fell slightly.

sophia (ml-infra): Expected: limiting buffer churn forces the compiler/runtime to pick different kernels — sometimes fused, sometimes not. Reuse can lower alloc churn but constrain available workspace which prevents some high-performance fused kernels.

adesh (eng-runtime): Proposal: route small-latency-sensitive traffic into a tight multipool slice with strict KV pinning + smaller workspace and keep a separate slice for large-seq models (opportunistic kernels, larger workspace). Add allocator metric vm_frag_pct to the console so we can act on fragmentation.

maria (runtime): I'll wire vm_frag_pct and try a second canary: multipool slice with fixed per-model KV caps + hybrid-slab workspace reduced to 32MB + reuse_buffers=true.

tomas (perf): Also capture kernel name per token in the trace (we have the hook). Add per-route p50/p95/p99 for token latency and include kernel_name histogram.

sophia (ml-infra): I'll spawn an adversarial mix generator (1x big generator + 4x small chats at realistic QPS) to stress swap and fragmentation. We should run 24h to capture slow drift.

maria (runtime): Thanks — I'll run the 24h canary and upload logs here. If the multipool pinning reduces swap_ops without hurting big-model throughput, we can add an automated fallback: when vm_frag_pct > 30% route to dedicated slice. :thumbsup:

adesh (eng-runtime): +1. After logs, we can try an additional change: make kernel selection aware of "pinned KV footprint" so it prefers kernels with smaller transient temps when pinned fraction > threshold.

maria (runtime): Noted. Action items: (1) wire vm_frag_pct to Console, (2) run 24h adversarial canary with reuse_buffers and workspace=32MB, (3) collect per-kernel memory high-water and kernel_name histogram, (4) evaluate pinning policy impact.

tomas (perf): I'll prepare the trace collection template and a small script that aggregates kernel memory HWM -> correlate with swap ops.

sophia (ml-infra): Setting up the adversarial mix job now. Will tag results in this thread.

maria (runtime): Great — I'll post interim logs in ~6h. Thanks everyone.
